note: Fixed translations for Termio's product vocabulary. Values come from the app's own Simplified Chinese UI strings (Sources/termio/Resources/Localization/zh-Hans.lproj), so a reader sees one word for one thing across the app and the docs. When a term is deliberately left in English — Agent, worktree, Hooks — that is the app's choice, not an omission. Translators and translation tooling must not paraphrase around these.
conventions: Terms: the `terms` map wins over anything that reads better. A term left in English there — Agent, worktree, hooks, Issues — is the app's own choice, not a gap to fill.

Leave untranslated: commands, code spans and blocks, file paths, config keys, URLs, MDX component calls (<Keybindings />), and product names. `~/.ssh/config` and `git worktree add` stay exactly as written.
Keyboard shortcuts keep the English page's glyphs and order, untranslated: ⌘1, ⇧⌘O, ⌘W.
UI strings must match what the app actually shows in Simplified Chinese, menu paths included: Settings ▸ Agents ▸ Live agent status becomes the app's own wording, never a fresh translation of it.
Structure is fixed: same heading levels in the same order, same lists, same table columns, same code blocks, same components. `pnpm docs:check` compares heading structure and fails on a mismatch.
Every heading other pages link to carries an explicit English id — `## 设备 [#device]` — so an anchor keeps working in every locale.
One half-width space between Chinese and Latin or digits (盘古之白): 多个编程 Agent 的终端. Chinese punctuation is full-width (。，：、「」), digits and Latin stay half-width, and an em dash is ——.
Voice: the English docs are direct, concrete and unshowy (see VOICE.md). Translate literally and keep that restraint — do not add emphasis, idiom or hedging the English does not have.
Translate what is there: no added explanations, no dropped sentences. Something true only for Chinese readers belongs in the English page first.
Front matter: keep `x-i18n.source_path` and refresh `source_hash` via `pnpm docs:stamp` after retranslating, so a stale page fails the build instead of drifting quietly.
